comments.text:
It would only have to go to Lake Granby in CO, which is where the CO river begins. From there, it could flow naturally to revitalize the river and its ecosystem, then the river can continue to service the southwestern US as the water system has been designed it to do. Then once the water reaches serviceable and more sustainable levels, the pipeline can be shut down, then operated only periodically, the way dams are used to control water flow. It would be more beneficial and less destructive to the environment than oil pipelines and as doable.

Given global warming, the further melting of northern polar ice regions, and off-and-on use of the pipeline, it would be centuries before any harm MIGHT come to the Great Lakes, if ever, because the Great Lakes are likely to continually be replenished more naturally than the waterways in the western US.

Of course, such projects will always be met by selfish haters who care only about themselves and blame everyone else for whatever or wherever a problem might be, which is a naive way of thinking. Because if the western US becomes unsustainable, then it WILL, 100%, affect the rest of the US, and then it will become a very serious problem for everyone. That's why Star Trek politics became necessary and eventually will have to become necessary in today's timeline, and projects like this could become one such necessary and doable project.
